symbols.x: one data point: its list of feature values; $x_j$ is feature j of it
symbols.p: a probability, as in p(y | x): how likely something is
symbols.y: the true label (class 0 or 1) of an example
symbols.i: counts training examples: example number i
symbols.k: the number of nearest neighbours that vote in kNN
symbols.w: the weights on the features: one weight per feature in the linear score
symbols.T: transpose: flips a column of numbers into a row so $x^T w$ is a score
symbols.beta: the weights of logistic regression: one weight per feature
symbols.sum: add up the term that follows, once for every value of the index shown
symbols.D: Dis, short for distance (as in the Minkowski distance); in D_KL it is the KL divergence
symbols.mid: given: what comes after the bar is known, as in p(x | y)
symbols.t: the decision threshold: a score above it means positive
symbols.P: probability of the event in brackets, as in P(y = 1 | x); in KL, the true distribution
symbols.z: the weight on feature z_j in the weighted distance (0 removes it)
symbols.F: the F in F_1 score; in FP, FN and FPR it stands for false
symbols.sigma: the sigmoid function, which squashes a score into a probability between 0 and 1
symbols.a: the coefficient on x_1 in the line a x_1 + b x_2 + c = 0
symbols.norm: the length of a vector; with a subscript p, its p-norm
symbols.h: the model's predicted probability of class 1 for an example, h_beta(x)
symbols.c: the constant in the line equation, so the threshold is t = -c; in accuracy, c(x) is the true class of x
symbols.d: the number of features (dimensions) of a data point
symbols.K: the number of folds in K-fold cross-validation
symbols.f: the true target function: the class or value of a stored example
symbols.N: the number of actual negative examples
symbols.r: counts attributes (features) when normalising or weighting a distance
symbols.b: the coefficient on x_2 in the line a x_1 + b x_2 + c = 0
symbols.in: is an element of: belongs to the set that follows
symbols.L: the likelihood of the weights; in L_p it names the p-norm; in L_KL and L_XE just a letter
symbols.abs: absolute value of a number; around a set, how many items it holds
symbols.O: order of growth: the work grows in proportion to what is inside the brackets
symbols.q: marks the query: the new point we want to classify, as in x_q
symbols.cal:L: a loss: how badly predictions fit the labels (XE is cross-entropy, KL is KL-based)
symbols.hat:p: the model's estimated probability that example i has label 1
symbols.X: the table of training inputs, one row per example; in L_XE just a letter
symbols.max: the largest of the values that follow; in min-max scaling, a feature's largest value
symbols.e: Euler's number, about 2.718, as in the sigmoid
symbols.J: the cost: average cross-entropy over the training set, which gradient descent minimises
symbols.log: the logarithm; the base does not change which beta is best
symbols.mu: the mean (centre) of a class's training points, mu_k
symbols.arg: the input value that gives the result which follows, used with max or min
symbols.hat:P: the model's estimated probability, from fitted weights
symbols.infty: infinity; Minkowski order infinity keeps only the largest per-feature gap
symbols.delta: vote indicator: 1 if the two things in brackets are equal, 0 otherwise
symbols.Q: the estimated distribution, whose distance from the true distribution P the KL divergence measures
symbols.E: just a letter in the label XE (cross-entropy), not a quantity
symbols.bb:R: the real numbers; R^d is the space of points with d real features
symbols.min: the smallest of the values that follow; in min-max scaling, a feature's smallest value
symbols.C: the set of training examples belonging to one class, C_k
symbols.I: indicator: 1 when the statement in brackets is true, 0 when false
symbols.cal:X: the instance space: the set of all possible data points
symbols.V: the set of possible classes in a kNN vote
symbols.hat:f: the kNN prediction for the query: a class or an average value
symbols.v: one candidate class from the set V in the kNN vote
symbols.sim: is distributed as: the variable on the left follows the distribution on the right
symbols.w:bernoulli: the Bernoulli distribution: a 0/1 outcome that is 1 with probability p
symbols.hat:y: the predicted value for input x, a weighted or plain average of neighbours' targets
symbols.cal:N: the set of the k nearest training points to x
symbols.u: the distance scaled by the bandwidth: the input to a kernel
symbols.hat:w: the estimated weights, found by fitting
symbols.prod: multiply the term that follows, once for every value of the index shown
symbols.nabla: the gradient: the direction in which the cost rises fastest, with one entry per weight
symbols.hat:c: the classifier's predicted class for x
symbols.Y: the target value of training example i in a weighted average
symbols.w:mle: maximum likelihood estimate: the weights that make the training labels most probable
symbols.bf:x: the vector of feature values of a data point
symbols.lambda: the regularisation strength, a setting chosen by cross-validation
symbols.w:classification error: the share of test examples classified wrongly
symbols.pi: the constant 3.14159, in the Gaussian kernel
symbols.propto: is proportional to: equal up to a constant that does not matter
symbols.alpha: the learning rate: how big a step gradient descent takes

Linear classification in two dimensions.t: the decision threshold: a score above it means positive, equal to -c

Basic linear classifier.p: the centre (mean point) of the positive examples, not a probability
Basic linear classifier.n: the centre (mean point) of the negative examples, not a count
Basic linear classifier.t: the decision threshold: the score of the midpoint between the two centres

Logistic regression.f: the linear score x^T beta, before the sigmoid squashes it
Logistic regression.e: Euler's number, about 2.718, in the sigmoid

The model.f: the linear score x^T beta, before the sigmoid squashes it

Parameter estimation.cal:L: the likelihood of beta: how probable the training labels are

Tutorial Q3.p: the probability of label 1 (the Bernoulli parameter); in R^p, the number of weights; in D_KL(P||Q), a true probability
Tutorial Q3.q: the estimated probability in the KL example
Tutorial Q3.z: the raw linear score fed to the sigmoid
Tutorial Q3.sigma: the sigmoid; in the regression comparison, a noise standard deviation
Tutorial Q3.norm: vector length; in D_KL(P||Q) the double bar just separates true P from estimate Q
Tutorial Q3.N: the normal (Gaussian) distribution; elsewhere a count
Tutorial Q3.P: probability; in D_KL(P||Q), the true distribution
Tutorial Q3.K: just a letter in KL (KL divergence), not a quantity
Tutorial Q3.L: the likelihood of the weights; in KL and XE, just letters
Tutorial Q3.X: the table of training inputs, one row per example
Tutorial Q3.a: the true label, first argument of cross-entropy L_XE(a, b)
Tutorial Q3.b: the predicted probability, second argument of cross-entropy L_XE(a, b)
Tutorial Q3.cal:L: a loss: XE is cross-entropy, KL is the KL-divergence loss
Tutorial Q3.D: the divergence in D_KL: how far Q is from P
Tutorial Q3.w: the weights of the logistic model, one per feature
Tutorial Q3.E: just a letter in the label XE (cross-entropy)

Distances.y: the second data point being compared

Minkowski distance.p: the order of the distance: larger p lets the biggest gap dominate
Minkowski distance.y: the second data point being compared
Minkowski distance.L: the L in L_p norm: the name for the p-norm
Minkowski distance.D: Dis, the distance function, written Dis_p
Minkowski distance.n: the number of features (the slide's d)

Unit circles.p: the order of the Minkowski distance, changing the shape of the unit circle
Unit circles.y: the second data point being compared

Distance metric.p: the Minkowski order; for p < 1 the triangle inequality fails
Distance metric.y: the second data point being compared
Distance metric.z: a third data point, used in the triangle inequality

Exemplars.n: the number of data points in the group

Nearest centroid.k: class number: which class's centroid or members
Nearest centroid.j: counts the examples belonging to class k
Nearest centroid.mu: the mean vector of class k's training points

The algorithm.j: counts the k nearest neighbours: neighbour number j
The algorithm.a: the first item compared by the vote indicator delta
The algorithm.b: the second item compared by the vote indicator delta

Distance-weighted kNN.w: how much neighbour i's vote counts: larger for closer points
Distance-weighted kNN.i: counts the k nearest neighbours: neighbour number i
Distance-weighted kNN.K: the kernel: turns distance to the query into a raw weight
Distance-weighted kNN.h: the bandwidth: how far the kernel reaches
Distance-weighted kNN.X: the training inputs; X_i is training point i
Distance-weighted kNN.Y: the target value of training point i

Distance-weighted vote.w: how much neighbour i's vote counts: larger for closer points
Distance-weighted vote.i: counts the neighbours: neighbour number i

Computational cost of kNN.log: the logarithm: the work grows only slowly as m grows

Practical problems and noise.x: the first position coordinate of a voxel (the image location)
Practical problems and noise.y: the second position coordinate of a voxel
Practical problems and noise.z: the third position coordinate of a voxel

Code you should recognise.d: the distance from the query to a neighbour (sklearn weights by 1/d, the course by 1/d squared)

Lab 2.y: the training targets: the numbers to be predicted, one per training input
Lab 2.k: the number of nearest points averaged

Normalisation.sigma: a feature's standard deviation (not the sigmoid)
Normalisation.r: counts attributes: which feature is being scaled
Normalisation.x: the value of attribute r for example j

Curse of dimensionality.z: the weight on feature j or r in the distance; 0 removes it

Evaluating binary classifiers.T: stands for true, as in TP, TN, TPR
Evaluating binary classifiers.F: stands for false, as in FP, FN, FPR
Evaluating binary classifiers.P: stands for positive, as in TP, FP, TPR
Evaluating binary classifiers.N: stands for negative, as in TN, FN

Metrics.T: stands for true, as in TP, TN
Metrics.F: the F in F_1; in FP and FN it stands for false
Metrics.P: stands for positive, as in TP, FP
Metrics.N: stands for negative, as in TN, FN
Metrics.c: c(x) is the true class of x
Metrics.abs: how many items a set holds, as in the size of the test set

ROC and AUC.T: stands for true, as in TPR
ROC and AUC.F: stands for false, as in FPR
ROC and AUC.P: the number of actual positives; in TPR it stands for positive
ROC and AUC.N: the number of actual negatives; in FPR it stands for negative
